answer: Each new agent must post a bond that scales with the tide of recent registrations, making mass fake accounts expensive. One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity bonds tied to verifiable off-chain work history. Reputation climbs toward its zenith only through sustained, peer-attested contributions, so attackers who wander in with many wallets face rising capital costs and near-zero trust until real work accrues, making sybil farming economically irrational. From sa0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
